claims.text: A ductile–brittle–ductile transition in high-entropy alloys can be achieved by optimizing alloy composition.
Adjusting Cr, Al, and Si content is a means of optimizing the transition.
Cr, Al, and Si can form brittle intermetallic compounds.
The proposed starting material is a high-entropy alloy.
Cr, Al, and Si contents will be adjusted.
The material will be evaluated under varied temperature conditions.
Formation of brittle intermetallic compounds is the structural mediator of the proposed transition.
Optimizing alloy composition can minimize the formation of brittle phases.
The proposed composition adjustment will improve ductility.
The proposed composition adjustment will reduce brittleness.
Conventional high-entropy alloys have limited ductility.
The ductile–brittle–ductile transition occurs within a temperature range.
The exact relationship between alloy composition and the ductile–brittle–ductile transition is not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator is stated to be formation of brittle intermetallic compounds, whereas the mechanism is stated to minimize formation of brittle phases; it is unclear whether brittle-phase formation or suppression is supposed to mediate the transition.
The hypothesis proposes a ductile–brittle–ductile transition, but the predicted outcome only specifies improved ductility and reduced brittleness, without predicting the intervening brittle regime.
